questions.question: Which one of the following CORRECTLY shows the relative charges of an electron, proton and neutron, respectively?
questions.explanation: Electrons have a negative charge (-1), protons have a positive charge (+1), and neutrons are neutral (0).

questions.question: According to Newton's first law, an object that is in motion continues its state of motion with

options.A: a decreasing speed if the resultant force exerted on it is zero.
options.B: constant velocity if the resultant force exerted on it is not zero.
options.C: an increasing speed if the resultant force exerted on it is not zero.
options.D: constant velocity if the resultant force exerted on it is zero.

questions.explanation: Newton's first law states that an object in motion will continue in motion with a constant velocity (both speed and direction) unless acted upon by a net external force. Thus, if the net force is zero, velocity is constant.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between distance and displacement?

options.A: Distance can be described both in magnitude and direction, while displacement is described only by magnitude.
options.B: Distance depends on the initial and final points, while displacement depends on the path followed by a moving body.
options.C: Distance is always greater than or equal to the magnitude of displacement, while the magnitude of the displacement is always less than or equal to distance.
options.D: Distance has either positive or negative values, while displacement has only positive value.

questions.explanation: Distance is a scalar quantity representing the total path length, which is always greater than or equal to the magnitude of displacement. Displacement is a vector quantity representing the straight-line distance and direction between initial and final points, so its magnitude is always less than or equal to the distance.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about a uniformly accelerated motion?

options.C: The speed is constant but the direction is changing.
options.D: The displacement increases at a uniform rate.

questions.explanation: Uniformly accelerated motion is defined as motion in which the acceleration remains constant throughout the motion. Velocity changes at a constant rate.

questions.question: Two displacement vectors have magnitudes 4 m and 3 m. Which one of the following is NOT the possible value of the magnitude of their resultant vector?
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the resultant of two vectors is between the difference of their magnitudes (|4-3|=1) and their sum (4+3=7). So, the possible range is 1 m to 7 m. 12 m is outside this range.

questions.question: A train is moving along a straight line with a constant acceleration of 5 m/s² when it passes by a traffic light point. From there on, if the time taken by the train to reach a velocity of 30 m/s is 4 seconds, then what is the distance of the train from the traffic point after 8 seconds?
questions.explanation: First, find initial velocity (u): v = u + at => 30 = u + (5)(4) => u = 10 m/s. Then, distance after 8 s: s = ut + (1/2)at² = (10)(8) + (0.5)(5)(8²) = 80 + 160 = 240 m.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is a necessary condition for an object to be in linear equilibrium?

options.A: The net force acting on the object is non-zero constant.
options.B: The linear acceleration of the object is zero.
options.C: The linear speed of the object is constant.
options.D: The linear acceleration of the object is non-zero constant.

questions.explanation: Linear equilibrium requires that the net force acting on an object is zero, which implies that the linear acceleration is zero. This means the object is either at rest or moving with constant velocity.

questions.question: When an object tends to slide over the surface of another object, tiny bumps at the surface of the two objects knocking and locking together. This causes
questions.explanation: Friction is a force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact. The microscopic interlocking of surface irregularities is a primary mechanism that causes friction.

questions.question: Suppose a ball is thrown vertically upward and after reaching a maximum height, it returns back to its initial position. Which of the following statement is correct about energy changes and work done on the ball?

options.A: On its way up, work done by gravity is positive.
options.B: On its way up, change in its kinetic energy is positive.
options.C: On its way down, work done by gravity is positive.
options.D: On its way down, change in its potential energy is positive.

questions.explanation: When the ball falls downward, gravity acts in the same direction as the displacement. Thus, the work done by gravity is positive. On its way up, gravity is opposite to displacement, so work done is negative.

questions.question: The mechanical energy of an oscillating object at any point through its path is equal to

options.A: the sum of its kinetic and potential energies.
options.B: the sum of its kinetic and internal energies.
options.C: the sum of its potential and internal energies.
options.D: the difference between its kinetic and potential energies.

questions.explanation: Mechanical energy is the sum of an object's kinetic energy (energy of motion) and potential energy (stored energy). In a conservative system, this total mechanical energy remains constant.

questions.question: A 2 kg object accelerates with 1.5 m/s² to the right on a horizontal frictionless surface under the action of two horizontal forces, F1 and F2 as shown in the figure below. (F2 = 1 N to the left). What should be the magnitude of F1?
questions.explanation: Using Newton's Second Law (F_net = ma), the net force is 2 kg * 1.5 m/s² = 3 N to the right. Since F2 is 1 N to the left, F1 must be 4 N to the right to give a net force of 3 N (4 N - 1 N = 3 N).

questions.question: A tennis ball of mass 0.10 kg traveling horizontally at 40.0 m/s is struck back by a racket. If the ball returns back with a speed of 30.0 m/s in the opposite direction, what is the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the ball by the racket?
questions.explanation: Impulse = change in momentum = m(v_f - v_i) = 0.10 kg * (30 m/s - (-40 m/s)) = 0.10 kg * 70 m/s = 7.0 kg·m/s.

questions.question: A force that is exerted on a simple machine in order to produce input work is called
questions.explanation: The effort is the input force applied to a simple machine to perform work. The load is the output force (or resistance) that the machine must overcome.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct about transverse and longitudinal waves?

options.A: The directions of wave motion and vibration of the particles are parallel for transverse waves and perpendicular for longitudinal waves.
options.B: Waves on a string are longitudinal whereas sound waves are transverse.
options.C: The directions of wave motion and vibration of particles are parallel for longitudinal waves but perpendicular for transverse waves.
options.D: A longitudinal wave comprises a series of crests and troughs, whereas a transverse wave comprises a series of compressions and rarefactions.

questions.explanation: In longitudinal waves, particles vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation (e.g., sound). In transverse waves, particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation (e.g., light, waves on a string).

questions.question: An object that is partially or fully submerged in a fluid experiences an upward force from the fluid. The apparent weight of the object is the weight of the

options.B: object in air minus the buoyant force.
options.D: fluid it displaces minus the buoyant force.

questions.explanation: Apparent weight is the actual weight of the object in air minus the upward buoyant force exerted by the fluid. This is why objects feel lighter when submerged.

questions.question: A force is used to push a box of mass, m along the slop of inclined plane with constant velocity as shown in the figure below. If the coefficient of friction between the box and the inclined plane be μ, the actual mechanical advantage (AMA) of the inclined plane is
questions.explanation: The effort F = mg(sin θ + μ cos θ). The load is mg. AMA = Load / Effort = mg / [mg(sin θ + μ cos θ)] = 1 / (sin θ + μ cos θ).

questions.question: A wheel and axle of radii 40 cm and 8 cm, respectively, is used to lift a bucket of 6 kg of water from a well by applying an effort of 20 N on the wheel. The percentage efficiency of this simple machine is
questions.explanation: IMA (Ideal Mechanical Advantage) = Radius of wheel / Radius of axle = 40 / 8 = 5. AMA (Actual Mechanical Advantage) = Load / Effort = (6 kg * 10 m/s²) / 20 N = 60 / 20 = 3. Efficiency = (AMA / IMA) * 100% = (3 / 5) * 100% = 60%.

questions.question: Block A of mass m1 = 8.0 kg travelling initially at u1 = 6 m/s in the positive x-direction collides with block B of mass m2 = 12 kg moving in the same direction at u2 = 3 m/s. If the velocity of block A, immediately after the collision, is v1 = 4 m/s to the positive x-axis, what is the velocity of the block B, immediately after the collision?
questions.explanation: Conservation of Momentum: m1*u1 + m2*u2 = m1*v1 + m2*v2. (8*6) + (12*3) = (8*4) + (12*v2). 48 + 36 = 32 + 12*v2 => 84 = 32 + 12*v2 => 52 = 12*v2 => v2 = 4.33 m/s. Since the result is positive, it moves in the positive x-axis.

questions.question: The amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a given substance by 1°C is
questions.explanation: Heat capacity is defined as the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of an entire substance (of a given mass) by 1 degree Celsius. Specific heat capacity is the amount of heat required to raise 1 gram of the substance by 1 degree Celsius.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct about the properties of waves?

options.A: When a wave is reflected, its speed and wavelength are changed.
options.B: When a wave is refracted, its speed and wavelength remain the same.
options.C: When two waves interfere destructively, the amplitude of the resultant wave is greater than the amplitude of each wave.
options.D: Diffraction of a wave through a narrow gap is more observable than through a wider gap.

questions.explanation: Diffraction is most pronounced when the size of the opening or obstacle is comparable to or smaller than the wavelength of the wave. A narrow gap causes more spreading of the wave than a wide gap.

questions.question: A square metal plate of coefficient of linear expansion α, has a surface area A0 at a temperature T0. If the temperature is raised by an amount ΔT, then the plate surface area is changed to A which is expressed as
questions.explanation: Area expansion (β) is twice the coefficient of linear expansion (α). The formula for area expansion is A = A0(1 + βΔT) = A0(1 + 2αΔT).

questions.question: The atmospheric pressure in a certain area is determined to be 103.36 kPa, using a mercury barometer shown in the figure below. (Acceleration due to gravity, g = 10 m/s², and density of mercury, ρ_m = 13.6 × 10³ kg/m³). The height to which the mercury column rises is about

An object dropped into a sea sinks to a depth of 100 m. Which of the following is correct about the pressure the object experiences? (Assume the density of seawater is 1030 kg/m³ and the air above the sea exerts a pressure of P_atmospheric = 1.00 × 10^5 Pa, g = 10 m/s²)

options.A: The absolute pressure exerted on it is P_absolute = 1.13 × 10^6 Pa.
options.B: The gauge pressure exerted on it is P_gauge = 1.03 × 10^7 Pa.
options.C: The gauge pressure exerted on it is P_gauge = 1.01 × 10^5 Pa.
options.D: The absolute pressure exerted on it is P_absolute = 9.30 × 10^5 Pa.

questions.explanation: Gauge pressure P_gauge = ρgh = 1030 * 10 * 100 = 1.03 × 10^6 Pa. Absolute P_abs = P_atm + P_gauge = 1.00 × 10^5 + 1.03 × 10^6 = 1.13 × 10^6 Pa.

questions.question: How much heat energy is required to change 5 kg of ice at -20°C to water at 10°C? (Specific heat capacities of water in liquid and solid phases are 4.2 kJ/kg·°C and 2.1 kJ/kg·°C, respectively, and latent heat of fusion of water, Lf = 336,000 J/kg).
questions.explanation: Heat ice from -20 to 0°C: Q1 = mc_ice ΔT = 5*2100*20 = 210,000 J. Melt ice at 0°C: Q2 = mL_f = 5*336,000 = 1,680,000 J. Heat water from 0 to 10°C: Q3 = mc_water ΔT = 5*4200*10 = 210,000 J. Total Q = Q1 + Q2 + Q3 = 2,100,000 J = 2.10 × 10^6 J.

questions.question: An electric field is defined as a region where

options.A: a neutral particle experiences electric force when it is placed in that region.
options.B: a charged particle experiences an electric force if it is placed in that region.
options.C: a charged particle losses its charge when it is placed in that region.
options.D: a charged particle experiences no electric force when it is placed in that region.

questions.explanation: An electric field is a region of space around a charged particle where another charged particle would experience an electric force.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct about the speed of sound in different medium? The speed of sound,

options.A: increases as the temperature and density of a material increases.
options.B: in liquid is less than its speed in gas.
options.C: in a colder and less dense medium is faster than in hotter and denser material.
options.D: in solid is less than its speed in liquid.

questions.explanation: The speed of sound is faster in warmer and denser media. Conversely, in colder and less dense media, sound travels slower. The general order of speed is: Solid > Liquid > Gas.

questions.question: Four resistors are connected to a voltage source as shown in the figure below. (R1 and R2 are in series, connected to a parallel combination of R3 and R4). Which one of the following is correct about the circuit?

options.A: R1 is connected in series with the effective combination of R3 and R4.
options.B: R2 is connected in parallel with the effective combination of R3 and R4.
options.C: R2 is connected in parallel with R3.
options.D: R1 is connected in parallel with R2.

questions.explanation: The circuit diagram shows that R1 and R2 are in series with each other, and the combination of R3 and R4 is in parallel with the R1-R2 series combination. Thus, R1 is in series with the parallel combination of R3 and R4.

questions.question: What is the magnitude of electric field strength at a distance of 2.0 m from a point charge, Q = 4.0 C? (Coulomb's constant, k = 9 x 10^9 Nm²/C²)

A wire that has a resistance of 6 Ω is drawn out so as to make it into a new wire two times as long as the original and half cross-sectional area of the original. What will be the resistance of the new wire?
questions.explanation: Resistance R = ρL / A. If the length L is doubled and area A is halved, the new resistance R_new = ρ(2L) / (A/2) = 4 * (ρL/A) = 4 * 6 Ω = 24 Ω.

questions.question: A long straight wire carries a current of 5.0 A. What is the magnetic field strength produced by the current at a distance of 2.0 cm from the wire? (Magnetic permeability of free space μ0 = 4π × 10⁻⁷ Tm/A)
If two vectors a→ and b→, with respective magnitudes of a and b, form an angle α between them when they are connected tail to tail, then the expression ab cos α defines the value of

options.A: scalar product of a→ and b→
options.D: vector product of a→ and b→

questions.explanation: The scalar (dot) product of two vectors is defined as a→ · b→ = ab cos α. This gives a scalar value, not a vector.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct about real and virtual images?

options.A: Real images can be magnified but virtual images cannot.
options.B: Virtual images can be magnified but real images cannot.
options.C: Virtual images can be displayed on a screen unlike the real ones.
options.D: Real images can be displayed on a screen unlike the virtual ones.

questions.explanation: Real images are formed when light rays converge and are found on the opposite side of the lens/mirror. They can be captured on a screen. Virtual images are formed where light rays only appear to diverge and cannot be projected onto a screen.

questions.question: An object moving in one dimension with constant acceleration a travels through a displacement s in a time interval t. If its velocity at the initial time t = 0 is vi and its velocity at a later time t is vf, which of the following is a correct relation between the given quantities?
questions.explanation: From vf = vi + at, we get vi = vf - at. Substituting into s = vi*t + (1/2)at² gives s = (vf - at)t + (1/2)at² = vf*t - at² + (1/2)at² = vf*t - (1/2)at².

questions.question: If the critical angle for an optically denser medium to air boundary is 53°, what will be the refractive index of the medium? (Assume the index of refraction of air is 1.00, sin 53° = cos 37° = 0.8, cos 53° = sin 37° = 0.6)
questions.explanation: Using Snell's law for critical angle: n_medium * sin(θc) = n_air * sin(90°). n_medium * 0.8 = 1 * 1 => n_medium = 1 / 0.8 = 1.25.

questions.question: Given the displacement vector A→ = (3î - 4ĵ) m, what is the unit vector in the direction of A→?
questions.explanation: Magnitude of A = √(3² + (-4)²) = 5 m. Unit vector = A / |A| = (3/5)î - (4/5)ĵ = 0.6î - 0.8ĵ.

questions.question: Suppose that you are given two forces with F1 = 75 N in the direction of 53° west of north and F2 = 100 N in the direction of 37° east of north. If you add the two forces using analytical and graphical methods and represent using graphical scale of 1 cm for 10 N force, what are the possible length and direction of the arrow line for the resultant vector?
questions.explanation: Component analysis: F1x = -75 * sin(53°) = -60 N, F1y = 75 * cos(53°) = 45 N. F2x = 100 * sin(37°) = 60 N, F2y = 100 * cos(37°) = 80 N. Resultant: Rx = -60 + 60 = 0, Ry = 45 + 80 = 125 N (due north). Graphical scale: 1 cm = 10 N, so 125 N = 12.5 cm to the North.

questions.question: Suppose a particle of mass, m is tied to a string and then whirled around in a horizontal circle of radius r about the center O as shown in the figure below. If the string makes an angle of θ to the vertical while rotating, the component of the force that is responsible for the circular motion of the mass by providing the centripetal force is
questions.explanation: The tension T has a vertical component T cos θ balancing gravity (mg) and a horizontal component T sin θ providing the centripetal force.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct about the fundamental forces in nature and their applications?

options.A: The force that keeps the nucleus of an atom from flying apart due to the repulsive force between protons is the weak nuclear force.
options.B: The gravitational force makes planets to revolve around the Sun and to follow their orbital path.
options.C: The force that arises in most radioactive processes and in nuclear reactions that generate the Sun's energy is the strong nuclear force.
options.D: The electromagnetic force is the force that keeps protons and neutrons bound together in the nucleus of an atom.

questions.explanation: The gravitational force is responsible for the attractive interaction between large masses, such as the Sun and the planets, which keeps the planets in their orbits.

questions.question: A spring stores 120 J of elastic potential energy when it is stretched by 0.5 m. What is the potential energy stored by the spring when it is stretched by 1.5 m?

The velocity-time graph of an object moving in a straight line is shown in the figure below. (Graph: velocity goes from -6 m/s at t=0, crosses 0 at t=2, peaks at 12 m/s at t=6, stays at 12 m/s until t=10, then drops to 0 at t=14). What is the magnitude of the total displacement covered by the object in the time interval of 14 seconds?
questions.explanation: Displacement is the area under the v-t graph. Area = -6*2/2 + 12*4/2 + 12*4 + 12*4/2 = -6 + 24 + 48 + 24 = 90 m. (Wait, the area calculation is complex. The initial displacement is negative). Let's calculate: Triangle 1 (t=0 to 2): 0.5*2*(-6) = -6. Triangle 2 (t=2 to 6): 0.5*4*12 = 24. Rectangle (t=6 to 10): 4*12 = 48. Triangle 3 (t=10 to 14): 0.5*4*12 = 24. Total = -6 + 24 + 48 + 24 = 90 m. The magnitude is 90 m. Please note there is an error in the original provided answer key which said 42 m. The correct calculated displacement is 90 m.

questions.question: A crane at port is used to lift 10,000 kg object to a height of 20 m. If the power developed by the crane is 50,000 W, how long does it take to lift the object? (Acceleration due to gravity, g = 10 m/s²)

A system of four masses m1 = 4 kg, m2 = 4 kg, m3 = 5 kg and m4 = 3 kg are located in the xy-plane at the coordinates of (0, 0), (30 cm, 0), (-40 cm, 0) and (0, 20 cm), respectively. What is the coordinate of the center of mass of the system?
Which of the following concepts of physics are the primary focus points in mechanical engineering?

options.B: Geometric optics, Electrostatics, Thermodynamics, and Stress
options.C: Molecular physics, Dynamics, Nuclear physics, and Force
options.D: Nuclear physics, Geometric optics, Dynamics, and Force

questions.explanation: Mechanical engineering is primarily concerned with the study of motion (Dynamics), energy (Thermodynamics), forces, and the mechanical properties of materials (Stress and Strain).

questions.question: Which one of the following defense technologies is correctly matched with its working principle?

options.A: A radar is a rocket propelled weapon designed to deliver an explosive weapon with a great accuracy at high speed.
options.B: Missiles radiate electromagnetic signal and examine the echo received to identify the location of the target.
options.C: Drones radiate electromagnetic signal and examine the echo received to identify the location of the target.
options.D: Infrared device uses heat emission to identify objects that cannot be detected using available light sources.

questions.explanation: Infrared (IR) devices detect the thermal radiation (heat) emitted by objects. This allows them to see objects in the dark or in conditions where visible light is not available.

questions.question: Which one of the following phenomena occurs during change of phases of a matter? During a phase change from

options.A: solid to liquid, heat energy is released from a substance while its temperature remains constant.
options.B: gas to liquid, heat energy is absorbed by a substance while its temperature remains constant.
options.C: liquid to gas, heat energy is absorbed by a substance while its temperature remains constant.
options.D: liquid to solid, heat energy is released from a substance while its temperature changes uniformly.

questions.explanation: During a phase change (e.g., liquid to gas), the temperature remains constant while the substance absorbs latent heat. The energy is used to break intermolecular bonds, not to increase kinetic energy (temperature).

questions.question: Assume that a ball is thrown horizontally from a building of height h above the ground with initial speed v0. Which one of the following statements is correct about the motion of the object?

options.A: Its vertical component velocity remains constant.
options.B: Its horizontal component acceleration is zero.
options.C: Its horizontal component velocity uniformly increases.
options.D: Its vertical component acceleration is zero.

questions.explanation: In projectile motion, the only acceleration is due to gravity (g) acting downward. Therefore, the horizontal acceleration is zero, and the horizontal velocity remains constant.

questions.question: A projectile is thrown from a level ground with an initial velocity v0 making an angle of θ above the horizontal. If the maximum height covered by the projectile is H, the what is the horizontal range of the projectile in terms of H and θ?
questions.explanation: Range R = v0² * sin(2θ) / g. Max Height H = v0² * sin²θ / (2g). Dividing R/H: R/H = (v0² * 2 sinθ cosθ / g) / (v0² * sin²θ / 2g) = (2 cosθ / sinθ) * 2 = 4 / tanθ. So R = 4H / tanθ.

questions.question: Four point masses m1 = 4 kg, m2 = 1 kg, m3 = 3 kg and m4 = 5 kg are attached to a massless rod which lays on the x-axis as shown in the figure below. (m4 is at x=-4m, m3 at x=-1m, m2 at x=2m, m1 at x=5m). How much is the moment of inertia of the system about the y-axis?
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia about the y-axis is I = Σ(m_i * x_i²). I = (4*5²) + (1*2²) + (3*(-1)²) + (5*(-4)²) = (4*25) + (1*4) + (3*1) + (5*16) = 100 + 4 + 3 + 80 = 187 kgm². (Note: The closest answer option is 184, likely due to a typo in the exam or the provided key).

questions.question: The flow rate of a fluid is defined as

options.A: the speed with which the fluid flowing through a pipe.
options.B: the volume of the fluid crossing an area per unit time taken.
options.C: the rate of change of the speed with which fluid flowing through a pipe.
options.D: the mass of the fluid crossing an area per unit time taken.

questions.explanation: Flow rate is the volume of fluid that passes through a given area per unit time (e.g., m³/s). The mass flow rate is mass per unit time.

questions.question: At normal condition, solids are almost incompressible compared to liquids and gases. The reason is that

options.A: their atoms are relatively fixed distance apart and held together.
options.B: their atoms are free to slide about and interact with neighbors.
options.C: there is much space and little force between atoms.
options.D: their atoms vibrate and free to move.

questions.explanation: Solids have a tightly packed structure with fixed atom positions held by strong intermolecular forces. This makes them difficult to compress. Liquids are slightly compressible, and gases are highly compressible due to the large spaces between particles.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about magnets?

options.A: Like electric charges, magnetic poles exist in a single isolated form.
options.B: The north pole of one magnet repels the south pole of another magnet.
options.C: If you cut a bar magnet into two, each piece has both north and south poles.
options.D: Unlike permanent magnets, electromagnets are magnets without poles.

questions.explanation: Magnetic poles always exist in pairs (north and south). If you cut a magnet, each piece will have its own north and south pole. Isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist.

questions.question: A wheel of radius, r = 50 cm, rotates about a fixed perpendicular axis that passes through its center. If the angular speed is ω = 200 rad/s, how much is the tangential speed of a point on the rim of the wheel?
questions.explanation: Tangential speed v = r * ω = 0.5 m * 200 rad/s = 100 m/s.

questions.question: Suppose your mass is measured to be 50 kg. If your friend having a mass of 55 kg is at a distance 2 m apart from you, what is the magnitude of gravitational force between you and your friend? (Universal gravitational constant, G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ Nm²/kg²)
A 10 N force is applied to the smaller circular piston of a hydraulic lift of radius 0.1 m to lift a 2500 N load placed on the larger piston. What is the area of the larger piston? (π = 3.14)
The magnetic field created by a long straight current carrying wire

options.A: is directly proportional to the distance from the wire.
options.B: is inversely proportional to the current in the wire.
options.C: is directed in the same direction as the current.
options.D: forms circular pattern around the wire.

questions.explanation: The magnetic field lines around a long straight current-carrying wire form concentric circles around the wire. The direction is determined by the right-hand rule.

questions.question: What will happen on a pure semiconductor when it is doped by group III element?
questions.explanation: Group III elements (like Boron, Aluminum) have only 3 valence electrons. When used to dope a Group IV semiconductor (like Silicon), they create 'holes' (positive charge carriers), making it a P-type semiconductor.

questions.question: We usually use plastic materials to cover metallic wires that carry electricity to protect living things from danger. Which of the following statement correctly describes the nature of the plastic to use for this purpose?

options.A: Since it has free electrons, it facilitates the easy flow of electric current in the metallic wires.
options.B: Since it has no free electrons, it directs the electrons in the wire to flow in the same direction.
options.C: Since every electron in plastic is slightly bound to the parent atom, it becomes poor conductor.
options.D: Since every electron in plastic is tightly bound to the parent atom, it becomes poor conductor.

questions.explanation: Plastic is an insulator because its electrons are tightly bound to the parent atoms. It has no free electrons to carry current, preventing electricity from flowing through it.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct about the current- voltage (I-V) characteristics of a typical semiconductor diode?

options.A: The current due to the minority charge carriers is represented in the forward bias region of the I-V curve.
options.B: The current due to the majority charge carriers is represented in the reverse bias region of the I-V curve.
options.C: The region of the I-V curve that rises very rapidly after the voltage exceeds the cut-in voltage is the forward bias region.
options.D: The region of the I-V curve that increases very rapidly after the bias voltage exceeds the breakdown voltage is in the forward bias region.

questions.explanation: In forward bias, once the applied voltage exceeds the cut-in voltage (e.g., 0.7 V for silicon), the current increases dramatically as the depletion layer narrows. This is the forward bias region.

questions.question: Consider a circuit containing diode and load resistor (RL) are connected to an AC voltage source as shown in the figure below. (A half-wave rectifier circuit). If initially, polarity of 'a' is positive while 'b' is negative,

options.A: During the first half-cycle, the diode is forward biased and voltage is developed across the load resistor.
options.B: During the second half-cycle, the diode is reverse biased and no current flow in the load resistor.
options.C: During the second half-cycle, the diode is forward biased and current flows in the load resistor.
options.D: During the first half-cycle, the diode is reverse biased and voltage is developed across the load resistor.

questions.explanation: When 'a' is positive and 'b' is negative, the anode of the diode is at a higher potential than the cathode, so it is forward biased. This allows current to flow through the load resistor, developing a voltage across it.

questions.question: A circular coil is located in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.50 T directed perpendicular to the plane of the coil. If the area of the coil changes with uniform rate, in such a way that it increases by 4.0 × 10⁻³ m² in 2 s, what is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force (emf) in the coil?
